key_insight: An explainable ML pipeline can discover a closed-form inductance formula that stays accurate even outside the training range for multilayer planar windings.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more reliable inductance sizing for high-frequency power converters, reducing dependence on costly FEM runs or brittle hand-derived formulas.
method: Post-hoc explainability with SHAP and permutation importance to identify influential winding features
SR-KAN symbolic regression using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to derive an analytical expression without preset formula structure
Validation on both large-scale FEA data and physical PCB prototypes to test extrapolation and real-world accuracy
evidence_signal: The study used over 10,000 FEA simulations across seven OOD classes and 55 PCB prototypes, with the SR-KAN model achieving 8.22% OOD relative error and 6.26% mean absolute relative error on hardware.
watch_item: The learned equation should still be revalidated when geometry, materials, or operating conditions differ substantially from the released dataset.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning for Multilayer Planar Winding Inductance Estimation
